topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: Repository layout should make dependencies and ownership easier to discover. HarborMetrics begins with a library that summarizes bounded integer measurements and a tiny executable that exercises its contract. The important separation is not the number of folders: it is whether the computational library can be built and tested without inheriting command-line parsing, global logging, or a particular deployment environment.

topics.title: 1.1.1 Separating Libraries from Applications
topics.summary: A library exposes operations that other code can call; an application chooses a policy for invoking them. Put a reusable summarize operation in the library and leave argument interpretation, terminal output, and exit codes in the executable. The library should report a result or a documented error rather than terminating the process itself.

topics.summary: A public header is a promise to consumers. Include only the types and declarations they need, make it self-contained, and avoid exposing implementation-only containers or platform headers without a reason. Private helpers can remain in an implementation file or a private include directory.

focus.title: Declare the interface
explain: This comment names the first file in the book’s combined listing. The packaged project contains that separate file.
#pragma once is a widely supported header guard directive; it asks the compiler to include this header once per translation unit.
The semicolon makes this a function declaration, with no body. It tells callers the parameter and result types.
focus.what: The header is the shared promise that a function named add accepts two ints and returns an int.
focus.where: Both .cpp files include this header during preprocessing.
focus.why: One public declaration prevents callers from inventing incompatible signatures.
focus.invariant: The definition must match this declaration. The project must supply exactly one external definition.
focus.risk: A header alone does not provide executable code for the function; omitting the implementation from linking leaves an unresolved symbol.

focus.title: Supply the definition
explain: This comment names the implementation file.
The include makes the public declaration visible to this translation unit.
The body defines add and returns the sum of its value parameters.
focus.what: The implementation supplies the code behind the declared interface.
focus.where: The compiler processes this .cpp separately; the linker later joins it with the caller.
focus.why: A private implementation can change while callers keep using the same interface.
focus.invariant: The fixture 20+22 fits in int and produces 42. In general, signed overflow must be avoided.
focus.risk: Copying the same non-inline definition into several .cpp files violates the one-definition rule.
